messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PAGER - High rate of token-introspect requests from unknown IPs to /auth/introspect (edge-proxy). Severity: P1. Channel: #incidents. Thread opened.
maya (oncall): Ack'd — I'm on it. Which edge region and sample IPs?
devon (infra): us-west-2 edge proxy. Src IPs: 45.77.182.19 and 45.77.182.20. Traffic spike ~11:42UTC, ~8k reqs/min combined. Many 401 -> immediate replay attempts. Logs show requests including X-Debug:true header attached.
irene (security): seeing 3 debug log files forwarded to telemetry bucket from staging-log-forwarder around the same time. The files contain truncated session identifiers and internal request IDs (not full tokens) but we should treat as potential PIIs until proven otherwise.
sam (runtime): grabbing samples now. Quick mitigation: block the two IPs at the edge WAF and drop X-Debug header in the proxy. Pushing a config change in 2m.
devon (infra): I'll push the WAF block. Applying rule now:
```
# edge-waf block
block ip 45.77.182.19/32
block ip 45.77.182.20/32
```
sam (runtime): done — proxy rejects from those IPs (503 -> 403). Also adding drop header rule:
```
proxy_set_header X-Debug "";
```
pagerbot: Incident created: INC-2026-3321. Pager owners: maya (oncall), devon.
maya (oncall): Good. devon/sam — can you confirm whether any customer session tokens were included in the forwarded files? Need quick exposure assessment for CS/legal.
devon (infra): I downloaded the three debug files (s3://redwood-telemetry/staging/debug/2026-03-17/). They have request logs with session_id fragments like "sess_4f3a***" and internal request ids. No full auth headers or bearer tokens in the samples I checked, just truncated ids and query params. I'm running a grep for 'Authorization' and 'Bearer' across the files now.
irene (security): If grep returns none, that lowers customer impact, but still rotate service account keys used by the log forwarder and revoke any presigned URLs from that window. Also mark those S3 objects for immediate restricted access and start scrub job.
sam (runtime): Commands I'm running now:
```
# rotate forwarder service account
rwdctl svcacct rotate --name staging-log-forwarder --scope telemetry
# remove forwarded debug files
aws s3 rm s3://redwood-telemetry/staging/debug/2026-03-17/ --recursive
# invalidate presigned urls (approx):
aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id E123ABC --paths "/telemetry/staging/debug/*"
```
devon (infra): grep result: no 'Authorization' or 'Bearer' strings. Only truncated session ids and internal IDs. Upload timestamps between 11:40:10 and 11:45:02 UTC.
cs_lead: prepping customer comms draft in case legal advises notification. Which customers had traffic from these IPs?
ops_shift: pulling reverse lookups now — mapping IPs -> destination hits on /v1/session and /v1/auth. Will post list in 5.
irene (security): Legal: please standby for potential low-impact notice. We need to rotate the staging-log-forwarder SA keys (sam doing) and produce a short timeline. If no tokens, ask CS to prepare optional notification with no action required.
legal: acknowledged. We'll wait for confirmed grep/no-auth then advise on wording. If any full tokens are found, escalate to immediate customer notification and compensatory measures.
maya (oncall): Good. Sam/devon, after rotation confirm key rotation succeeded and list files removed. Also add a short-term retention policy to prevent debug uploads from staging to telemetry without an approval flag.
sam (runtime): rotation succeeded, new keys propagated. Deleted the three debug objects and created a deny policy for bucket write from staging-log-forwarder until approved. Pushing follow-up PR to require env var REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_ALLOW_DEBUG=true to allow debug-level uploads.
devon (infra): WAF blocks active, proxy header drop active, S3 objects removed, rotation done. Creating a short runbook entry and tagging this incident for postmortem.
pagerbot: Update: severity remains P1 until runbook actions complete. Next update due in 30m.
maya (oncall): Assigning follow-ups: irene -> postmortem/impact assessment, sam -> runbook+PR, devon -> WAF/proxy change audit, cs_lead/legal -> customer comms draft + approval. I'll take incident lead until resolved.
cs_lead: Draft ready, will wait for legal signoff. Suggest phrasing: "We detected anomalous traffic to our edge and an internal debug log forward. We removed the files and rotated internal keys. No customer action required at this time."
irene (security): I'll run an additional sweep for correlated IPs in other regions and check honeypot telemetry for similar X-Debug abuse vectors.
ops_shift: I've added a temporary alert (rule id 0087) to detect any future uploads with debug=true to telemetry buckets and page on first occurence.
maya (oncall): Thanks team. Keep updates short. Next full update in 30m or earlier if we see customer-impacting evidence. :thumbsup:
